transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this medication-safety huddle before I sign off on the afternoon decision regarding the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol. As you know, the protocol was introduced Monday, the medication is stocked in the automated dispensing cabinets, and orders are going through the electronic medication record. Before we proceed to using this on the night shift, I need each of your areas to report any operational findings. I'd like to start with pharmacy, then laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical IT. Please share anything relevant to the safe use of this protocol.

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern from pharmacy. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. These errors occurred at the point of selection from the automated dispensing cabinets. As a potential safeguard, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the ADCs and instead supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold, which would eliminate the risk of concentration selection errors at the bedside.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From laboratory medicine, I need to report that our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This is important for the group to be aware of before we proceed with the night shift.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From nursing education, I need to report a critical staffing concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they are permitted to administer this medication. This is a significant operational issue that needs to be addressed before we proceed with using the protocol on the night shift.

transcript.text: From clinical IT, I can report that I've confirmed a high-priority electronic medication-record alert can be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert would warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released. This serves as an additional electronic safeguard to support safe use of the protocol on the night shift.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on bedside ADC stock of the anticoagulant; pharmacy-prepared syringes only during the interim period to eliminate concentration selection errors at the point of care.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Standardize to pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes only, with no bedside stock of the 2 mg/mL concentration in the ADCs during the temporary hold.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: aPTT testing every six hours as the approved replacement for anti-Xa monitoring until the anti-Xa analyzer is available for calibration on Friday at 17:00.
decisions.nurse_authorization: Charge-nurse sign-off required for any nurse who has not completed the new anticoagulant administration module before they are permitted to administer this medication on tonight's shift.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today to warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before order release.

Ensure charge-nurse sign-off is enforced for all 18 nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module before they administer this medication tonight.
Deploy the high-priority concentration selection alert in the electronic medication record at 16:00 today with mandatory acknowledgment before order release.
